messages:
elena: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands runtime section — wanted to surface a few clarifying Qs for the team. Mainly around batching/caching tradeoffs and kernel rollout timing. Can we thread answers here?

ajay: Happy to start. Short answers first, then details if folks want them.

michael: On batching: what's our target latency impact (p50/p99) when continuous batching is enabled for chat workloads? Customers worry about tail latency.

ajay: Target is roughly +8–12ms p50 and +30–50ms p99 vs single-request baseline for typical 4k-token workloads when continuous batching is on. That assumes batch sizes in the 16–64 range and no KV cache hit.

sara: Are those numbers assuming prefix/KV caching? Also how do we measure p99 — end-to-end (app->response) or inference-only?

ajay: Good call. The numbers I quoted are inference-only. With a warm prefix cache hit we often see p99 improve by 20–60% depending on hit rate. End-to-end p99 includes network/queuing and so is +~10–40ms more depending on routing.

ben: Important ops note: prefix caching will be route-configurable. We'll default to opt-in for customer routes that explicitly allow cross-request caching. No global surprise caching on.

elena: That helps. For kernel work — two quick asks: 1) rollout schedule for the fused-attention kernels? 2) any compatibility risk for quantized models?

priya: Kernel v3 (fused attention + tiled GEMM) starts canary next Tue in us-west-2 on 2 GPU machines. Canary window 72h, then ramp to 10% over the following week if no regressions. We'll keep an automatic fallback to v2 on latency regressions.

michael: Any special metrics to watch during canary so we can call it fast? I can add dashboards.

priya: Yes — watch these three: 1) per-host token/s, 2) p99 inference latency, 3) quantized_model_failures (error rate for q4/q8 paths). If quantized failures >0.1% or p99 increases >15% we auto-roll back.

ajay: Also watch memory oversubscribe counts (kernel v3 uses slightly different allocation strategy) — add `host_mem_fragmentation` graph.

ops-bot: Reminder: canary deploy scheduled: 2026-02-03T09:00:00Z -> 2026-02-06T09:00:00Z. Auto-rollback: enabled.

sara: Quick question on caching consistency for user sessions: if we cache prefixes across requests, how do we avoid leaking across tenants or users?

ben: Cache keys are composed of (customer_id, route_id, prefix_hash). No cross-tenant leakage. For sensitive routes customers can disable prefix caching.

ajay: Also for privacy we TTL per-prefix entries aggressively (default 5m) and support route-level overrides.

michael: Can you paste the minimal runtime config snippet we plan to expose in Console so SREs can test locally?

priya: Sure — example:
```
# runtime route config example
batching: 
  continuous: true
  max_batch_size: 48
  latency_slo_ms: 60
cache:
  prefix_cache: 
    enabled: true
    ttl_seconds: 300
    scope: route
kernel: 
  preferred_version: v3
  fallback_to: v2
```

ajay: Note: `latency_slo_ms` is advisory for the autoscaler and kernel scheduler — it's used to tune batch windows.

elena: Awesome. One last leadership Q we got: how will these runtime changes affect Dedicated customers vs Hosted? Any differences in defaults?

ben: Defaults differ — Dedicated will stay conservative: continuous batching off by default, prefix cache off by default, kernel v3 optional until customer opt-in. Hosted defaults gradually move to the new settings after we've validated canaries and 10% ramp. We'll announce a migration window and provide an explicit opt-out flag.

michael: Will communicate to customers and add migration docs + sample scripts.

priya: We'll post a canary report in #eng-runtime after the 72h window with perf graphs and any rollbacks.

elena: Thanks everyone — please keep updates short here. If you need to coordinate a game-time rollback runbook, ping me and ops and we'll join. :thumbsup:

ajay: Thanks — will follow-up with a thread that includes dashboard links and alerts to subscribe to.

ops-bot: Note: incident playbook `runtime-canary-rollback` was updated 2026-01-28.

ben: Adding a small checklist for the docs team to publish: migration notes, route config examples, and FAQ on cache privacy. I'll spin a PR today.

elena: Perfect. Closing the thread unless new questions show up here.
